public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative search is not reliable enough and does not yet have a clear business model.

statement.excerpt: The initially-celebrated use case of “generative search” isn’t reliable enough (and doesn’t yet have a clear business model).
statement.document_title: When Will the GenAI Bubble Burst?

from_speaker: doesn’t yet have a clear business model
our_interpretation: The ordinary reliability reading is that users cannot consistently trust generated search answers and their supporting sources without material verification. It does not demand perfect accuracy.

In the surrounding discussion of costs and revenue, a clear business model means a credible, economically viable way to earn money from generative search. An advertised subscription or an advertising experiment alone does not establish that.
Viability need not mean current profitability. Credible evidence that customer payments or advertising can sustainably cover delivery and other relevant costs can establish a viable model.
Use the first calendar quarter of 2024, ending on the post date, as the latest reporting window for this ongoing industry observation.
Assess reliability and commercial viability separately. Weak evidence on one component cannot settle the other.
This is an industry-level commercial proposition, not a stated financial metric for a particular company; metric_scope is therefore null.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations show consequential, recurring reliability failures in ordinary generative-search use, and commercial evidence establishes that a credible sustainable business model remained unsettled.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations establish adequate reliability for ordinary search use, or evidence establishes a clear viable commercial model for a substantial generative-search offering. Revenue mechanisms alone, and the mere absence of current profits, settle neither condition.

evidence.explanation: Alphabet describes an identifiable advertising approach and favorable early feedback, which weighs against treating generative search as lacking any commercial direction. The disclosure does not connect SGE advertising returns to its delivery costs, so it does not establish or disprove viability under the contract.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative evaluations of first-quarter 2024 search answers, together with contemporaneous evidence connecting customer demand and monetization to the costs of providing generative search.
